claims: A G3 (Strong) geomagnetic storm is a significant disturbance in Earth’s magnetic field caused by solar activity, such as a Coronal Mass Ejection (CME).
As of March 2026, G3 conditions have driven auroras far south of their usual polar regions.
As of March 2026, auroras have potential visibility in northern U.S. states.
During a G3 storm, aurora (Northern Lights) may be visible as low as Illinois.
During a G3 storm, aurora (Northern Lights) may be visible as low as Oregon.
During a G3 storm, prime viewing of aurora is in northern states like Michigan, Maine, and Washington.
G3 geomagnetic storms can affect satellites and power grids.
Major disruption from G3 geomagnetic storms is rare.
During a G3 storm, high-latitude power systems may experience voltage alarms.
During a G3 storm, satellites in low-earth orbit can experience increased drag.
During a G3 storm, GPS and radio signals can experience intermittent issues.
The storm is occurring early in 2026.
The storm involves high-speed solar winds.
Effects of the storm sometimes last over a day.
